headline: A stand-in for the lunar maria in Saudi Arabia's Harrat Khaybar
summary: A 61 km window on the basalt plateau north of Medina matches Mare Tranquillitatis in 4 of the 5 dimensions we can test: terrain, surface, dryness and rock type. Only temperature fails. It is the only site in the detailed tier to match four dimensions for any lunar region (it does so for Marius Hills as well, 4 of 5). The gridded scan put it in the top 0.05% of Earth's land without knowing its rock type; an independent geological map then confirmed Neogene basalt, which lifts it to rank 1 of 121 listed sites.
why: Lunar surface missions will drive across basaltic plains and hope to shelter in lava tubes. Today's basaltic training grounds are wetter and partly vegetated (our blended rainfall estimate: Iceland 895, Hawaiʻi 1284, Idaho 317 mm/yr against 41 here). A dry, bare, dark basalt plateau with mapped lava tubes and mare-like slopes at kilometre scale is a candidate for long-traverse rover trials, tube-exploration rehearsals and work on basalt as a construction or oxygen feedstock.
differences: Temperature is the failed dimension: 299 K mean with a 29 K daily swing, against 217 K and about 300 K at the Apollo 11 site. Gap closure is 3%.
Albedo 0.10 against 0.07: young basalt and thin soil are brighter than mature mare regolith, and a peak NDVI of 0.13 shows sparse seasonal vegetation.
The ground is lava flow and scoria, not metres of impact-gardened regolith. Grain shape, glass content and electrostatic dust behaviour are not reproduced.
The field also holds silica-rich lava domes (Jabal Abyad, Jabal Bayda) with no mare counterpart.
About 41 mm of rain a year, wind, and a full atmosphere at 1 g.
Slopes are compared over a 3.8 km baseline. Metre-scale lava roughness, which governs rover hazard, is not assessed.

literature.claim: Geological map units at the point: “Cenozoic volcanic rocks” — mafic volcanic rocks; basalt (Neogene). This lookup is independent of the scan.
Umm Jirsan, inside Harrat Khaybar, is reported as the longest known lava tube in Arabia at 1,481 m — a process feature our scan cannot see.
literature.source: Stewart et al. 2024, PLOS ONE (reported by Live Science)

literature.claim: The lunar counterparts are documented: an intact lava tube beneath the Marius Hills skylight and a cave conduit beneath the Mare Tranquillitatis pit.
literature.source: Kaku et al. 2017, Geophys. Res. Lett. 44, 10155; Carrer et al. 2024, Nature Astronomy 8, 1119

literature.claim: Harrat Khaybar is one of the large Cenozoic basalt fields of western Arabia, with eruptions continuing into historical times.
literature.source: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program, Harrat Khaybar

novelty: Not among the 26 established analog sites in our validation list (nearest: Negev — Makhtesh Ramon, 765 km). A web search on 13 November 2026 for Harrat Khaybar or the Saudi harrats as lunar or planetary analogs returned geological, archaeological and geoheritage studies and visual comparisons, but no analog-science or mission-simulation study. That is what one search found, not proof that none exists. Confidence is moderate: across perturbed runs its percentile ranges 92.9–100.0.

headline: The closest match to Jezero Crater is a 5,200 m desert in the West Kunlun
summary: The single best-scoring land cell on Earth for Jezero, under 4 of 5 mission profiles, is a bare plateau at 35.4°N 82.6°E between the Kunlun and Karakoram ranges. It holds that position in the stress tests (percentile 99.96–100). Terrain and surface match almost exactly (albedo 0.171 against 0.173; median slope 1.29° against 1.19°). Against the established Qaidam Basin site 853 km to the east it scores 0.94 vs 0.69 on terrain, 0.27 vs 0.19 on thermal, 0.97 vs 0.73 on surface and 0.56 vs 0.62 on aridity. It still matches only 2 of 6 dimensions outright: cold, thin air and geology are partial.
why: The published case for the Qaidam Basin as a Mars analog rests on being high, cold, dry and bare. The scan applies that same logic with numbers and finds that it points several hundred kilometres further west, to ground that is higher, colder and at least as dry. For hardware, that means roughly half sea-level pressure, seven frozen months and Jezero-like slopes in one place.
differences: Mean surface temperature 270 K against 224 K: 30% of the gap from typical Earth land. The daily swing is 25 K against 85 K.
Pressure 53 kPa is about half of sea level and still roughly 74 times Jezero's 0.72 kPa.
About 59 mm of precipitation a year, seasonal snow, and 5 months with mean temperatures above freezing: liquid water occurs here.
Geology is known to us only from a 1:50M-scale map unit (Mesozoic sedimentary rocks). Nothing here shows the delta, carbonate and olivine-rich assemblage that makes Jezero scientifically important.
Above 5,000 m and far from roads. Whether field work is practical is a separate question the scores do not answer.

literature.claim: The region between the Kunlun and Karakoram is described as the coldest and driest part of the Tibetan Plateau, with precipitation near 50 mm/yr. Our blended satellite–reanalysis estimate at the cell is 59 mm/yr.
literature.source: Fort & van Vliet-Lanoë, Permafrost and periglacial environment of Western Tibet, Landform Analysis

literature.claim: A 2025 permafrost study treats the West Kunlun as a 55,669 km² region of “extreme cold arid conditions”. It is a permafrost study, not a planetary one.
Recognised Mars analogs lie on either side: the Qaidam Basin and Ladakh. Both were held out of scoring and land at percentile 99.9 and 99.6 for their best region.
literature.source: Xiao et al. 2017, Earth-Sci. Rev. 164, 84; Pandey et al. 2020, Int. J. Astrobiol. 19, 78

novelty: Not among the 26 established analog sites in our list (nearest: Ladakh — Tso Kar / Puga, 467 km). Our search found the West Kunlun studied for permafrost and glaciers but not as a planetary analog. The environmental reasoning is not new, since it is the published case for Qaidam. What is new is a quantitative ranking that places this ground above both neighbouring analog provinces.

headline: Mongolia's Gobi: a terrain twin for the lunar maria, only a partial one for Mars
summary: The challenge brief asks about the Gobi, so we tested it directly. Its best cell, in southern Ömnögovi at 42.9°N 101.4°E, is the top-ranked land cell on Earth for Mare Tranquillitatis in the gridded scan: median slope 0.68° against 0.69°, relief 671 m against 615 m, roughness scaling 0.95 against 0.96, on dark, bare ground. For Mars, the best Mongolian cell for each region sits between percentile 95.8 and 100.0 but matches at most 2 dimensions. The Gobi earns its place on terrain and surface, not on climate.
why: Mongolia is developing its own analog station in the Gobi. These numbers suggest where that effort is on firm ground, namely mobility, navigation and operations on plains shaped like lunar maria and the flatter Martian sites, and where a claim of Mars-like climate would not survive measurement.
differences: Rock type: the mapped unit is Paleozoic sedimentary and felsic volcanic rock, not basalt, so geology scores 0.40.
Albedo 0.13 against 0.07 for mare regolith: dark for a desert, still nearly twice as bright.
About 77 mm of precipitation a year. That is arid, not hyper-arid; aridity scores 0.50.
Mean surface temperature 282 K, with a warmest month near 302 K. Against Jezero this closes 11% of the thermal gap.
The comparison is at kilometre scale. Gravel pavement, vegetation patches and dry channels at rover scale are not assessed.

literature.claim: MARS-V, a Mongolian organisation, is developing a Mars analog station in the Dundgovi–Ömnögovi Gobi and describes the region as highly Mars-like. We found no published quantitative basis for that comparison.
Geological map unit at the point: “Paleozoic sedimentary and volcanic rocks” — felsic volcanic rocks.

Best Mongolian cell per Mars region (percentile of Earth's land, dimensions matched): Valles Marineris 100.0 (2); Jezero Crater 99.8 (2); Meridiani Planum 99.8 (2); Arsia Mons flank 99.8 (1); Elysium Planitia 99.8 (1); Gale Crater 99.3 (1); Utopia Planitia 97.6 (2); Arcadia Planitia 95.8 (1).
literature.source: This analysis, gridded scan, balanced profile

novelty: That the Gobi resembles Mars is an existing claim. What this adds is measurement: which part of the Gobi, similar to which planetary region, in which dimensions, and by how much. The lunar-mare terrain match was not something our search found proposed elsewhere. Confidence for the lunar match is high (percentile 95.6–100 under perturbation).
